> Hello everyone,
>
> I'm quite new to R-SWAT and I've been attempting sensitivity and calibration of SWAT+ using R-SWAT. I have a few questions related to the R interface:
>
> Why do different TxtInOut folders exist in the working directory when selecting parallel threads? How can I determine the optimal simulation parameter value from these folders?

R-SWAT copy the input TxtInOut to different folder to run parallel, depending on number of threads you used. Ex. if you use 4 threads, there will be 4 folders TxtInOut with number from _1 to _4

>
> What is the significance of the input behavioral threshold? I noticed it's set as -0.5 in a YouTube tutorial. Could you explain the reasoning behind this choice?

-0.5 just an example, don't take it for granted. You could search in the literature review what is the acceptable behavioral thresholds (it varies case to case)

>
> When defining the model output for extraction, does the column correspond to the channel where the gauge station is located? Similarly, does Reach number 1 represent the reach for that particular channel?

 The column indicates output variables (e.g., streamflow, please see SWAT+ documentation for this), reach number indicates location of the gauge station

>
> To identify the most sensitive parameter among the 20 available parameters, how many iterations should I aim for? Should I opt for 1 parallel processing or 4 (considering my system supports only four nodes)?

There is no concrete answer how many runs you need, need to do convergence test (e.g., just try different number of iterations until you don't see changes in the sensitivity ranking)
